thread:
maya: @here Heads-up — Nimbus (org:nimbus-prod) reports repeated 429s during their nightly sync. Window is narrow (~30–45s) and happens every hour at :58. They sent a sample response header showing Retry-After. Can we confirm which limit is getting hit and quick mitigations? :eyes:

raj: Can you paste the response headers and a short summary of their traffic pattern (concurrency, qps spikes)? Also want the org id and route they hit.

maya: Yep, headers from their client (redacted):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 9
x-rw-ratelimit-per-minute: 120
x-rw-ratelimit-per-minute-remaining: 0
x-rw-ratelimit-burst-window-seconds: 60
X-Request-Id: abcd-1234
```
They say ~10 workers, each opens multiple concurrent streams. We see ~2.4k requests/min at peak in their logs (they called it a "sync storm").

sarah: That looks like a per-minute cap exhaustion with a short burst window. If remaining=0 and Retry-After is present, the gateway is telling them to back off for ~9s. Question: are they doing any client-side retry jitter/backoff or hammering on retry without jitter?

maya: Customer says they used simple linear backoff + immediate retry on 429. No jitter. Their client code: `for i in 0..3 { if 429 => sleep(5); retry }`.

ingrid: Two quick mitigations for them: 1) add exponential backoff + randomized jitter on retries, 2) smooth out the sync by sharding across the minute boundary (spread requests over 60s instead of batch in 10s). Also ask if they can enable streaming/batch endpoints to reduce request count.

raj: I'll also check cluster-side metrics for that org/route to verify whether it's the global per-minute bucket or a per-route rate cap and whether there's traffic folding from upstream proxy. Can someone attach proxy logs / client request pattern?

maya: Uploading a short sample of their request cadence from their side (timestamps truncated):
```
2024-05-12T00:57:58Z client=nimbus worker=1 concurrent=25 reqs=600
2024-05-12T00:58:02Z client=nimbus worker=2 concurrent=30 reqs=700
2024-05-12T00:58:12Z client=nimbus worker=5 concurrent=40 reqs=1000
```
They admitted they batch a lot at the same minute mark.

sarah: That explains it — leaky-bucket/per-minute capacity gets drained quickly when you concentrate so many requests inside the burst window. Short Retry-After implies it's the minute-window refill behavior.

ingrid: Actionable checklist for immediate customer guidance: 
- Implement exponential + jitter backoff (eg: base=500ms, factor=2, jitter=uniform 0.5–1.5x)
- Lower per-worker concurrency or add client-side queueing to cap steady QPS to ~60% of their quota (so they don't hit 0 remaining)
- Spread sync across full minute or use a token bucket client-side
- If they need sustained higher throughput, propose Dedicated capacity or a quota increase (requires support escalation + billing confirmation)
- Respect Retry-After header and avoid tight retry loops that amplify spikes

raj: For our side, I'll pull per-route rate-limit graphs and edge logs for org=nimbus-prod between 00:56–01:02 UTC and check if requests were folded by an upstream proxy (some customers use a small proxy that fans out). Will report back here.

support-bot: Automated runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/429-ratecap (contains client/backoff examples, replay steps, and template customer email). :white_check_mark:

maya: I'll send the customer the checklist and ask for proxy logs/trace ids. Also asking them to try a local replay that spreads requests over 60s to confirm it fixes the 429s.

sarah: One more note — if they include an X-Client-Id header we can better attribute requests in the future and route them to a warmer KV cache; suggest they add it.

maya: Copy. Will push those recommendations. Leaving this thread open until we get the proxy logs and our per-route metrics. :thumbsup:

raj: Update — pulled the graphs: clear spike at :58, per-minute quota dropped to 0 for two consecutive minutes. No evidence of upstream folding. I recommend a temporary quota bump while the customer implements smoothing.

maya: Thanks — I'll open the quota request and attach the graphs. Closing only after customer confirms reduced 429s.

ingrid: If they want a faster workaround, we can enable a short canary quota increase for one hour (ops approval needed).

maya: Request filed with ops. Will post ticket id once approved.
